name: Woodtech
old_description: Datatek's origins date back to 1988 when we began making blue line prints for the architectural/engineering trades under the name of Alabama Blueprint & Supply Co, Inc. Moving forward with changes in digital technology, the little company traded the ammonia-vapor "blue-print" machines for state-of-the-art digital printers. The change resulted in increased capabilities and additional job positions. The company has continued its growth in the local market and is the oldest operating full-service reprographic company in the region.
about:
Woodtech, a division of Datatek, was launched in early 2014 in Huntsville, Alabama. Datatek traces its roots to 1988 when it began as Alabama Blueprint & Supply Co., Inc., producing blue line prints for architects and engineers. The company transitioned to digital printing in the 2000s and expanded into custom signage with a flatbed printer in 2007. Woodtech emerged to combine digital printing with fine woodworking, opening a retail showroom in the Clinton Row project downtown.

Woodtech operates a production facility offering CNC woodworking, digital flatbed printing, and custom finishing. Services include custom signage, furniture, inlays, overlays, framing, and polyurethane coating. The shop sources reclaimed lumber from Madison County and North Alabama, partnering with local artists for design input. A partnership with Swampworks Amplifiers adds custom-built, printed amplifiers to the lineup. The facility supports both one-off custom pieces and repeat production runs.

Customers span construction, architecture, engineering, real estate, fine art, photography, education, and brewing industries. The company serves businesses needing jobsite signs, presentation boards, retail-ready home décor, gift items, and custom furniture build-outs. Local breweries, schools, and retail shops are cited as repeat clients.

Woodtech emphasizes a local supply chain, using wood from naturally felled trees and collaborating with regional artists. The division was started to merge digital printing capabilities with woodworking, creating customizable yet scalable products. The downtown showroom provides a direct retail channel while the production side serves B2B orders.
